items.stem: The interquartile range is
options: the upper quartile minus the lower quartile
the upper quartile plus the lower quartile
the largest value minus the smallest
the median minus the lower quartile
items.answer: the upper quartile minus the lower quartile
items.markingKey: IQR = Q3 − Q1.

items.stem: The 50th percentile of a data set is the same as
items.markingKey: Half the data lie below it.

items.stem: Explain why the interquartile range is often preferred to the range as a measure of spread.
items.answer: The range uses only the two extreme values, so an outlier changes it a lot; the IQR covers the middle half of the data and is not affected by extreme values.
items.markingKey: B1 range depends on extremes; B1 IQR uses middle 50% / resistant to outliers [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) If y = (x − a)/b with b > 0, then the standard deviation of x is (b) The variance of x is given by

items.stem: For 37 values, Σ(x − 20) = 8 and Σ(x − 20)² = 1178. Hana finds the standard deviation of the coded values and then adds 20, giving 25.6. Explain the error and state the correct standard deviation of x.
items.answer: Subtracting 20 does not change the spread, so 20 should not be added back to the standard deviation: σ = 5.64.
